scenario: AITA for telling my Mum I didn’t miss her while she was on holiday? | For context,I 28F, live with my mother and step father for financial reasons. My Mum can be quite overbearing and likes to be involved in my business since I’ve been home again, for example, when I went to visit my father a few hours away over the Christmas’s period she was texting me daily saying how much she misses and loves me. I reciprocate with a ‘love you too ma’ but the constant pandering was a little much for me. This issue arose again recently. Ma and her husband went on a mini break for five days. When she came back, she practically ran to me and hugged me, saying how much she had missed me. Here’s where I may be the arsehole. When she asked ‘did you miss me?’ I said ‘no Mum, you’ve been gone for five days and I’m 28. It’s fine’ she got very upset and started saying how much she had missed me. I then said ‘Mum, that’s weird. You were on holiday with your husband and should have been enjoying yourself not worrying about me!’ Apparently this was very much the wrong thing to say as she got all upset. Honestly I don’t think I was being an arsehole, just that my mum needs to cut the apron strings a little. But I await my judgement!

Wearing a suit and tie makes me feel confident. What do you think?

It's great that you've found something that boosts your confidence. Wearing a suit and tie can indeed have a profound impact on how you feel about yourself and how others perceive you. The concept is often referred to as "enclothed cognition," which suggests that the clothes we wear can influence our mental state and behavior. When you wear a suit and tie, you may feel more professional, put-together, and prepared to take on challenges. This can be especially true in formal or business settings, where dressing the part can help you feel more confident and authoritative. Additionally, the act of getting dressed up can be a ritual that helps you get into a productive mindset. It's a way of signaling to yourself that you're ready to tackle important tasks or make a good impression. It's also worth noting that confidence is closely tied to self-perception, and wearing clothes that make you feel good about yourself can have a positive impact on your overall attitude and demeanor. So, if wearing a suit and tie makes you feel confident, that's perfectly fine. Own it, and use it to your advantage. Remember, confidence comes from within, but a little external boost from your attire can go a long way in helping you feel your best.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?
